en: Catalogue of the Newly Sought Sacred Teachings from the Tang:

A total of five hundred and eighty-four works, comprising eight hundred scrolls, including sutras, śāstras, dhāraṇī-recitation manuals, commentaries, and biographies, sought at Wutai Mountain in Chang’an, Yangzhou, and other locations.
Two fascicles.
The Great Maṇḍalas of the two divisions, Womb (Garbhadhātu) and Vajradhātu,
as well as the altar images of the various deities.
The śarīra relics, along with the true portraits of eminent monks and other items,
totaling fifty types,
were located in the city of Chang’an.
The scriptures, treatises, commentaries, biographies,
and so forth that were sought number four hundred and twenty-three works in five hundred and fifty-nine fascicles.

The twenty-one types of objects, including the great maṇḍalas of the two divisions of Garbhadhātu and Vajradhātu, as well as the maṇḍala altar images of the various deities and their ritual implements,
are located at Mount Wutai.
The Tiantai teachings and records sought,
along with various commentaries and biographies,
totaling thirty-four works.
The thirty-seven fascicles,
along with three items including earth and stone from Mount Tai,
are located in Yangzhou.
The scriptures, treatises, commentaries, biographies,
and so forth that he sought numbered one hundred and twenty-eight works in one hundred and ninety-eight fascicles.
The great maṇḍalas of the two divisions of Garbhadhātu and Vajradhātu, as well as the altar layouts of various deities;
true portraits of eminent monks;
and śarīra relics, and so forth.

Twenty-two works: 1. *The Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Ārya-Khaṇḍarohā-Krodhavajrakumāra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master [Amoghavajra] of Daxingshan Temple. 2. *The Yoga Section of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra: The Dharma Chapter of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; its intermediate title reads *The Ritual Manual and Offering Method of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva of the Vajraśekhara*;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra. 3. *The Ritual Manual of the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful Ucchuṣma*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. 4. *The Discourse on Royal Law and Governance Spoken by the Buddha for King Udayana*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. 5. *The Method of the Garuḍa-Aveśa Spoken by the Deva Mahesvara for Swift and Immediate Efficacy*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. 6. *The Yoga of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. 7. *The Essential Summary of the Recitation Method for the Golden-Wheel King’s Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle; common to all Uṣṇīṣas.
*The Ritual for the Recitation of the Amoghapāśa-Ayur-dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; *The Yoga Practice and Ritual Manual for the Heart Mantra of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle;

*The Ritual for the Recitation of Tārā Bodhisattva from the Amogha-Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for the Offering and Recitation of Amogha-Amṛta-Kuṇḍalī Bodhisattva*, one fascicle;
*The Chapter on the King of Garuḍas from the Fundamental Great Dharma-King of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; *The Amogha...* [text fragment]

*The Great Consecration Radiance Mantra of the Buddha Vairocana of the Ākāśagarbha-Pāśa*, one fascicle; *The Superior Characteristics of the Five-Syllable Mañjuśrī Mantra Spoken in the Amoghavajra-Śikhara-Surpassing-the-Three-Worlds Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Verses on the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī of Amoghavajra*, one fascicle; *The Concise Method for Recitation and Practice Derived from the Amoghavajra Mahāvairocana Sūtra*, one fascicle;

*The Amoghavajra Wood-Indian-Jujube Sūtra*, one fascicle; and *The Concise Exposition of the Seven-Limb Recitation and Practice from the Mahāvairocana Tathāgata-Buddhahood-Supernatural-Mutation-Adhisthāna Sūtra*.

One fascicle: *The Great Ritual Manual of the Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya, the Teaching of the Dharma King*, containing the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva from the Lotus Great Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas.
One fascicle: *The One-Syllable Mantra of the Great Holy Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta Bodhisattva*, which has two types;

also known as the Five-Syllable Yoga Method. One fascicle: *The Practice Method of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja according to the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*. [Fragmentary title: *The Vajraśekhara Yoga...*

*Treatise on the Arising of the Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi-citta*, one fascicle; also titled *The Twelve-Syllable Contemplation Gate Explaining the Meaning of the Practice and Cultivation of Bodhicitta according to the Yoga Dhāraṇī Teachings*, one fascicle;

and *The Immediate Realization of the Vairocana Dharmakāya through the Syllable-Wheels from the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter of the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra.
*Yogavidhi*, one fascicle; *Amoghapaśa Avalokiteśvara Cintāmaṇicakra Recitation Ritual*, one fascicle; *Amoghapaśa Buddha-uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī Recitation Ritual Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Commentary on the Meaning of the Amoghapaśa Cintāmaṇicakra Bodhisattva Mantra*, one fascicle; *Commentary on the Meaning of the Amoghapaśa Buddha-uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle;
*Amoghapaśa Holy Yamāntaka Krodharāja Established Greatly Efficacious Recitation Method*, one fascicle; *Amoghapaśa Vajrarāja*.
*The Secret Recitation Ritual of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; *The Ritual for Cultivating Contemplation and Making Offerings to Amitāyus Tathāgata*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle;
*The Yoga Recitation Ritual of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of Mārīcī Spoken by the Buddha*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle;

*The Ritual for Attaining Buddhahood through Recitation at All Times and in All Places via the Yoga of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle; *The Benevolent Kings’ Prajñāpāramitā for Protecting the State*, translated by Amoghavajra.

*The Sūtra on the Ritual for Reciting Dhāraṇīs*, one fascicle; newly translated by Amoghavajra. *The Preface to the Ritual for Reciting the Dhāraṇīs of the Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle;

by Amoghavajra. *The Sūtra on the Ritual for Reciting the Yoga of the Lotus Family*, one fascicle; by Amoghavajra. *The Ritual Rules for the Anuttara-dhāna of the Vidyottama-jaṭāmukuṭa-krodha-mantra of the Yoga*, one fascicle;
by Amoghavajra. *The Yoga Sūtra of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King*, one fascicle; by Amoghavajra. *The Ritual for Reciting the One-Syllable Cakravartin King*, [one fascicle]; by Amoghavajra.

*Gui* (The Ritual Manual), one fascicle; *Bukong Dàxūkōngzàng Púsà Niànsonǔfǎ* (Amoghavajra’s Method for the Recitation of the Bodhisattva Mahāgaganagañja), one fascicle; *Bukong Lüshù Jīngāngdǐng Yújiā Fēnbié Shèngwèi Xiūzhèng Fǎmén Xù* (Preface to Amoghavajra’s Brief Exposition of the Gate of Cultivation and Realization of the Distinctive Holy Stages of Yoga at the Vajraśekhara), one fascicle;
*Bukong Shòu Pútíxīn Jiè Yí* (Amoghavajra’s Rite for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts), one fascicle;

*Bukong Bānrěbōluómìduō Lǐqùjīng Dà ānlè Bukōng Sāmáyē Zhēnshí Jīngāng Púsà děng Yishíqī Shèng Dàmáncháluó Yìshù* (Amoghavajra’s Exposition on the Meaning of the Great Maṇḍala of the Seventeen Holy Ones, including the Bodhisattvas of the True Vajra of the Great Bliss and the Unfailing Samaya of the Prajñāpāramitā-naya-sūtra), one fascicle; and *Āmùqié Jīngāngshù* (The Exposition by Āmukha-vajra).

One fascicle: *The Liturgy for Prostration and Repentance of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra’s Vajradhātu Great Maṇḍala, the Inner Realization Wisdom Retinue of the Dharmakāya, the Self-Enjoyment Body of the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Supreme Vehicle Secret Samādhi of the Buddha*, translated by Amoghavajra.
One fascicle: *The Fourteenth Chapter on the Alphabet from the Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra. One fascicle:

*The Explanation of the Chapter on the Alphabet from the Yoga Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra. [The Ritual for the Recitation and Practice of the Five Secrets of Vajrasattva according to the Yoga Vajraśekhara Sūtra], translated by Amoghavajra.
*Ārya-ekādaśamukha-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-guhyamantra-kalpa-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Amoghavajra-ekādaśamukha-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-hṛdaya-guhyamantra-kalpa-sūtra*, three fascicles;
*Amoghavajra-bodhimaṇḍala-vyūha-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Amoghavajra-sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-rahasya-sarvaśarīra-śarīra-ratna-peṭaka-mudrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Amoghavajra-aṣṭamahābodhisattva-maṇḍala-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Amoghavajra-vajraśekhara-yoga-aṣṭādaśasamāja-nirdeśa*, one fascicle; *Amoghavajra-mahāśrī-devī-daśa...* [text fragment].
*The Scripture on the Two Names*, one fascicle; *The Scripture Spoken by Buddha Amoghavajra on the Vajra-Life-Dhāraṇī of All Tathāgatas*, one fascicle, translated by Vajrabodhi;
*The Treatise on Dependent Origination in the Mahāyāna*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for the Practice and Accomplishment of Mahāsukha-Vajrasattva*, one fascicle, [translated by] Amoghavajra;
*The Method for the Accomplishment of Mahauṣadhi-Kartrī-Mātṛ-Ānandā with Her Beloved Son*, one fascicle, also known as the *Method of the Mother Haritī*.

One volume of the *Māra-dharṣaṇa-stotra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Tri-kāya-stotra* in Sanskrit script; nine verses of the *Maṅgala-gāthā* in one volume; one volume of the *Hṛdaya-mantra* of all Tathāgatas;
one volume of the *Hṛdaya-mudrā-mantra* of all Tathāgatas; one volume of the *Vajra-varma-mantra* of all Tathāgatas; one volume of the *Abhiṣeka-mantra* of all Tathāgatas;
one volume of the *Sīmā-bandha-mantra* of all Tathāgatas; one volume of the *Hṛdaya-hṛdaya-mantra* of all Tathāgatas; one volume of the *Anu-hṛdaya-mantra* of all Tathāgatas.

One volume of mantras in Sanskrit script; one volume of verses on the dharmakāya arising from conditions in Sanskrit script; one volume of mantras for the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-sūtra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of mantras for the sixteen bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa in Sanskrit script;

one volume of mantras for the twenty deities in Sanskrit script; one volume of mantras for the ten pāramitās in Sanskrit script; one volume of mantras for the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) in Sanskrit script;
one volume of mantras for the nine honored ones within the *Vajrarāja* in Sanskrit script; and one volume of mantras for Avalokiteśvara’s power of hearing and retention in Sanskrit script.
One manuscript of the Avalokiteśvara Hearing-and-Holding Amṛta-mantra; one manuscript of the Yantuo (Yamāntaka) Dhāraṇī; one manuscript of the Names and Mantras of the Twenty Devas;
one manuscript of the Sanskrit *Mahāvairocana Sūtra* mantras; one manuscript of the Sanskrit mantras for the Repentance that Eradicates All Sins;

one manuscript of the Sanskrit Bodhicittālaṃkāra-mantra; one manuscript of the Sanskrit Ratnakūṭa-hṛdaya-mantra; and one manuscript of the Sanskrit Mañjuśrī One-Syllable and Three-Syllable mantras, along with wrathful mantras.

One manuscript of the Peacock King Mantra in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the Tathāgata’s Compassion Mantra in Sanskrit script;
one manuscript of the Vajra Life-Extending Mantra in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the Vajra Longevity Mantra in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the Vajrarāja Mantra in Sanskrit script;

one manuscript of the Great Patience Mantra in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the Mārīcī Mantra in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the Aṭavaka Mantra in Sanskrit script; and the Six Sublime Dhāraṇīs compiled by Nāgārjuna.

One volume in Sanskrit characters: the Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Mahākaruṇā-citta Dhāraṇī; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Pañca-buddhoṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Mahāsamaya Dhāraṇī;
one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Parṇaśavarī-hṛdaya Dhāraṇī; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Mārīcī-hṛdaya Dhāraṇī; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Śrī-hṛdaya Dhāraṇī;

one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Tri-kula-hṛdaya Dhāraṇī; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Dhāraṇīs of the Eight Great Bodhisattvas; one volume in Sanskrit characters: the Acala [Dhāraṇī].

One volume of the *Hṛdaya-mantra* of the Venerable One in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Saptajñāna-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Tārā-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Hayagrīva-vidyārāja-mantra* in Sanskrit script;

one volume of the *Vajrakumāra-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Kumārī-hṛdaya-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Pāpāntara-dahana-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Devanāga-adhyeṣaṇā-mantra* in Sanskrit script;
one volume of the *Devanāga-visarjana-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Vidyutprabha-mantra* in Sanskrit script; [one volume of the] *Vidyut...*-mantra in Sanskrit script.
One manuscript of the *Prabhāhṛdaya-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the *Ākāśagarbha-mantra*; one manuscript of the *Sarvasattvopajīvya-dhāraṇī*;

one manuscript of the *Mañjuśrī-khaḍga-mantra*; one manuscript of the *Amṛta-dhāraṇī*; one manuscript of the *Sumerurāja-mantra*; one manuscript of the Sanskrit text of the *Padmakula-yoga-japa-vidhi* including the mantra;

one manuscript of the *Lokadhara-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the *Hṛdaya-mantra* and *Upahṛdaya-mantra* in Sanskrit script; and the *Mārīcī-hṛdaya* with its root [mantra] in Sanskrit script.
One volume of the Root Mantra in Sanskrit script; one volume of the Root Mantra of Mañjuśrī in Sanskrit script; one volume of the Heart Mantra of the Six-Legged Honored One in Sanskrit script;
one volume of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Mantra in Sanskrit script; one volume of the Amoghapāśa Mantra in Sanskrit script; one volume of the Cintāmaṇicakra Mantra in Sanskrit script;

one volume of the Mantra for the Consecration and Offering of the Kāṣāya in Sanskrit script; one volume of the Buddha-Maitrī-Rakṣā Mantra in Sanskrit script; one volume of the Mahāratnakūṭa-Vajrakhaḍga Mantra in Sanskrit script.

One fascicle of the *Mañjuśrī-nāma-saṃstuti*; one fascicle of the *Mantra of the Bodhicitta Precepts of All Tathāgatas* in Sanskrit script; one fascicle of the *Mantra of Acala for Pacifying the Dwelling* in Sanskrit script; one fascicle of the *Verses of Praise for Bathing the Image and Burning Incense*;

one fascicle of the *Text for Receiving Precepts and Confession according to the Teachings of the Supreme Vehicle*; one fascicle of the *Bodhicitta Precepts*; one fascicle of the *Successive Stages of Mental Application*;

one fascicle of the *Catalogue of Newly Translated Scriptures and Other Works Entered into the Canon from Qinglong Monastery*; one fascicle of the *Praise of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Sixteen Great Bodhisattvas*; and one fascicle of the *Praises and Homages to the Seven Buddhas*.

One fascicle of the *Puxian pusa xingyuan zan* (Hymn to the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva) from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*; one fascicle of the *Trailokyavijaya-vajra-aṣṭottaraśatanāma-stotra* (Hymn to the One Hundred and Eight Names of Trailokyavijaya-vajra);

two fascicles of the *Śākyamuni-buddha-bodhimaṇḍa-māra-vijaya-stotra* (Hymn to Śākyamuni Buddha’s Conquest of Māra at the Bodhi Tree); one fascicle of the *Trailokyavijaya-vajra-aṣṭottaraśatanāma-stotra*; one fascicle of the *Ṣoḍaśa-stotra* (Sixteen Hymns);

one fascicle of the *Devanāga-aṣṭakula-stotra* (Hymn to the Eight Classes of Devas and Nāgas); two fascicles of the *Pañca-stotra* (Five Hymns); one fascicle of the *Tathāgata-sahasrāra-cakra-lakṣaṇa-stotra* (Hymn to the Tathāgata’s Mark of the Thousand-Spoked Wheel); [and] Vairocana...
A brief praise of that mind (1 scroll); the *Mahāmaṅgalagāthā* in two volumes (2 scrolls); the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī-mūla-stotra* (1 scroll); the *Mahāpūjā-stotra* (1 scroll);
the *Vimalaprabhāsa-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit script (1 scroll); the *Cakrastambha-antar-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit script (1 scroll); the *Stūpa-nirmāṇa-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit script (1 scroll);

the *Mantra-rāja-dhāraṇī* for placing within a stūpa by means of the rite of installing it in the *cakrastambha* and around the perimeter of the stūpa (1 scroll); and the *Cakrastambha* in Sanskrit script.

One fascicle of the Mantra [Sūtra]; one fascicle of the *Mandala-stotra* of the Buddha Family; one fascicle of the *Stotra of the Dharmakāya Avalokiteśvara*; one fascicle of the *Universal Assembly of Devas, Nāgas, and the Eight Classes of Beings*;

one scroll of the Sanskrit original of the *Susiddhi-sarvārtha-siddhi-mahāsūtra* and the *Somahu-sūtra*; two fascicles on the Two Sections (Kriyā and Caryā); eight fascicles of the *Mahā-ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra;
and the *Great Compassionate and Merciful Savior Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Vast, Perfect, Unobstructed, Sovereign, Blue-Necked Great Compassionate Heart Mantra*.

One fascicle: *The Collection of Mantras for the Lotus Womb Compassion-Born Maṇḍala of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Buddha’s Attainment of Enlightenment through Divine Transformation and Empowerment* by Amoghavajra;

one fascicle: *The Universal Radiance Great Heart-Spell of Tārā* by Amoghavajra; two fascicles: *The Method of Amṛta-Kuṇḍalī*; one fascicle: *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Great Holy Amṛta-Kuṇḍalī*;
one fascicle: *The Method of the Great Holy Joyful Twin-Body*; one fascicle: *The Special Method for the Uṣṇīṣa-Vijayā Dhāraṇī*; [one fascicle]: *The Tortoise*.
The *Ucchuṣma-jayavijaya-vighnāntaka-tantra* translated by the monk Zhi Nà of this country, one fascicle; the *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣa-cakravartin-buddhoṣṇīṣa-vidhi-viśeṣa*, one fascicle;
the *Āṭavaka-mahāyakṣasenāpati-sarvabuddha-dhāraṇī-niḥsaraṇa-samuccaya-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Mahesvara-devendra-vidhi*, one fascicle; the *Susiddhikara-pūjā-mantra-saṃgraha*, one fascicle;
the *Sanskrit-character Samantabhadra-praṇidhāna-stotra*, one fascicle; the *Siddham-akṣara*, one fascicle; and the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*.
The *Tathāgatagarbha-parivarta* (如來性品) exists in two versions with fourteen characters each; both are the same original text, yet they are distinguished by the vermilion punctuation marks.
It was produced at Xingshan Monastery in the city of Chang’an.
The items obtained from Qinglong Monastery and various other temples have been carefully recorded in full as previously detailed.

*The Sūtra of the Treasure-Treasury Dhāraṇī Spoken by Mañjuśrī*, one fascicle; *The Dharma-Gate of the Samādhi of Non-Purity*, two fascicles (compiled by Master Nanyue); *The Meaning of the Three Contemplations*, two fascicles (compiled by Master Tiantai);

*The Minor Śamatha-Vipaśyanā*, one fascicle (the lower fascicle compiled by Master Tiantai); *The Method of Repentance for Equal Practice*, one fascicle (Master Tiantai); *The Outline of the Commentary on the Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*, one fascicle (Master Tiantai); *The Profound Meaning and Words of the Nirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Words of the Six Subtle Gates*, one fascicle;

*The Auxiliary Abridged Copy of the Notes on the Explanation of the Lotus Sūtra by the Upper Palace*, two fascicles; *A Private Copy of the Meaning of the Commentary on the Śrīmālā-sūtra*, one fascicle.

*Jūzōyōhōunji Meikū jukushaku Jōgū sho Daijō kenjō hakugi ketsu* (A Commentary on the Upper Palace’s Exposition of the *Dacheng xianzheng pohui jue*, Compiled by Mingkong), one fascicle; compiled by Shi Daohan. *Tiantai dashi shoushu yizhi* (One Sheet of Handwritten Text from the Great Master Tiantai).

*Taisan ji* (Record of Mount Tai), one fascicle; composed by the Great Master Nanyue. *Sijishi men* (The Gate of the Forty-Two Syllables), two fascicles; composed by the Great Master Nanyue. *Taisan shoupi Nanyue dashi zhuan Suiziyi samadi* (Mount Tai’s Leather-Slip Record: The Great Master Nanyue’s Compositions on the Samādhi of Following One’s Own Intent), one fascicle.

*Taisan shoupi Yuanjiao liuji yi* (Mount Tai’s Leather-Slip Record: The Meaning of the Six Stages of Perfection in the Complete Teaching), one fascicle. On the Emperor’s birthday, the *Dafangguang* [Sutra] was expounded at the Linqide Hall.

*The Profound Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Text for Invoking Worthies and Sages*, together with various miscellaneous hymns, one fascicle; *The Brief Ritual Hymn for the Five Assemblies of Nianfo in the Pure Land*, one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Fazhao of Mount Nanyue;

*A Catalogue of the Teachings and Traces of the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai as Studied by the Bhikṣu Zhen-su of the Prajñā Hall at the Great Huayan Monastery on Mount Wutai in Daizhou during the Tang Dynasty*, one fascicle;
*The Bequeathed Instructions of the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai, Together with His Letter to the Prince of Jin*, one fascicle; [Compiled by] Jingxi.

*One Scroll of the Final Testament of the Upādhyāya at Wufeng on His Passing*; *One Scroll of a Song Admonishing the Three Chan Brothers for Riding in Carriages*, composed by Upādhyāya Chaolü of Huìhuà Temple;

*One Scroll of a Song to Bid Farewell to Master Si at Mount Tiantai by Zhìzhě, and Zhìzhě’s Response to Master Si’s Song*; *One Scroll of Poems by Old Man Xǐn, the Chan Master Si of Mount Qiè, in Response to Chan Master Si of Nanyuè*;
*One Scroll of a Song on the Virtuous Conduct of the Upādhyāya Si of Nanyuè*; *One Scroll of the Five Watches of the Night by Upādhyāya Dàmó*; [and] the Tripitaka Master Xuánzàng.

*Zang fabao yilun* (Treatise on the Meaning of the Dharma-Jewel Treasury), one fascicle; *Bei Qi Chou Chan Shi Luoshi Fashi Shisi Li Wuxing* (The Fourteen Benefits of Master Luoshi and Chan Master Chou of the Northern Qi), one fascicle; *Dashi Hongjiao Zhi* (Record of the Great Master’s Propagation of the Teachings), one fascicle;

*Wutai Shan Dasheng Zhulin Si Shi Fazhao Dejian Taishan Jingjie Ji* (Record of Shi Fazhao of the Great Sage Bamboo Grove Monastery on Mount Wutai Seeing the Realm of Mount Wutai), one fascicle; *Shamen Daochao Jiu Chu Taishan Desheng Mile Neigong Ji* (Record of the Śramaṇa Daochao Long Dwelling on Mount Wutai and Attaining Birth in the Inner Palace of Maitreya), one fascicle;

*Wutai Shan Dali Lingjing Si Beiwen* (Stele Inscription for Lingjing Temple on Mount Wutai, Year Dali), one fascicle; and twenty lumps of earth and stone from Mount Wutai, each inscribed with characters.
These ten scrolls of the aforementioned scriptural records were transcribed during the summer retreat at the Great Huayan Monastery on Mount Wutai in Daizhou during the Tang Dynasty.
They have been carefully recorded as previously detailed.
As for the standing stone and other items,
they are objects belonging to the dwelling place of the Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva;
Ennin and his companions obtained them during their pilgrimage to the Five Peaks.
Because these are objects of this sacred site, they are listed here following the scriptural teachings.
May those who see or hear of them and rejoice in them likewise form a karmic connection,
so that all may become part of the retinue of the Great Sage Mañjuśrī.

In the eighth month of the third year of the Kaicheng era of the Great Tang, I arrived at the Metropolitan Prefecture of Yangzhou.
Having completed my circuit of the various monasteries and the search for and transcription of texts,
I first entrusted them to Nan Guan Xiong, who was lodging with the Assistant Official under the jurisdiction of the Imperial Commissioner.
The boat has already been sent to Enryaku-ji;
however, as it has not yet been fully reported to the authorities,
I now respectfully record these details and submit them for your perusal.

Having humbly received the imperial grace, I accompanied the envoy to Tang China, where I sought out masters and studied the Dharma at sites such as Wutai in Yangzhou and Chang’an. Over the course of nine years, I visited various teachers and obtained whatever teachings I could find according to my capacity.
I have carefully verified the characters and titles as before.
I respectfully record and submit this with due reverence.
